Theme 052 · Signature directions

Depth / 3D

Every scene is built from translucent glass plates floating in perspective — the launch-film language of dev-tool companies. The hook explodes a stack of dashboards along the Z axis, the drop slides four ghost planes into one flat lockup, and the proof separates two layers that never merge: your dashboard below, the Pulse audit layer hovering above it.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Glass plate — white 74 % + bright inner edge + hairline + deep soft shadow, r22 — the only surface type
  • Exploded stack — one 3D rig, plates 120–150 px apart in Z, joined by dashed rails
  • Z-rails — 3 px dashed teal lines along the depth axis; make the space legible
  • Ghost echoes — outlined teal copies of the wordmark that stream forward and lock into one plane
  • Audit layer — glass panel hovering ~300 px above the floor table; a coral drop-line pins the anomaly to its cell
  • Depth collapse — end state: all angles 0°, Z 0, two hairline echoes as a memory of the depth

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Plate fly-in — translateZ −400 → 0 with 20° → 0° tilt, expo.out 0.6 s, one plate per beat (0.5 s at 120 BPM)
  • Camera orbit — rig rotateY −34° → −28° + dolly 8 %, sine.inOut over 2 bars (4 s) — keeps the stack alive between hits
  • Drop-line pin — coral line draws 0 → 100 % in 0.25 s (power2.in) exactly on a bar downbeat, followed by a 2-ring ripple 0.4 s

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

Depth makes an invisible “background” product physical: the viewer literally sees Pulse as a layer above their own tools, which is the positioning in one image. Risk: text on tilted planes loses legibility — keep numbers on the flattest plane, cap tilt at 30° and never tilt the headline.

Adapt to your product: Put your customer’s existing tool on the floor plate and your product as the hovering glass layer; any audit, copilot or observability product maps 1:1. Replace the plate contents with your own real screens exported as flat PNG/HTML.

References: https://stripe.com/blog/connect-front-end-experience (3D CSS planes and cubes in a product launch page) · https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/perspective (how CSS perspective builds a shared 3D space) · https://css-tricks.com/how-css-perspective-works/ (perspective vs. perspective-origin in practice)
